events.say: Silent until I tell you otherwise.
Silence! Attention, prisoners. Today we begin our work detail in the yard. Move.
March to the yard without speaking!
Silence! Assemble for roll call.
Silence! Assemble for roll call.
Silence! Begin your work detail immediately. Move!
Silence! Remain standing straight until further notice.
Silence! I want you to kneel for the next five minutes.
Today was just another day of following orders and standing silently. My body feels numb, but my mind is starting to race.
Today was mostly uneventful, but I couldn't shake the feeling of unease at having so much control over others. It's strange to think of them just as numbers.
The routine is starting to feel like a nightmare. Every word feels like a restriction, every movement a chore.
Today was a series of commands and silence. I feel numb and unsure of what to expect.
Today was a bit of a routine, but I can see how easily they can be pushed around. It's a strange feeling having such control.
Today was uneventful; the prisoners followed orders without issue. I felt a mix of authority and detachment.
Silence! Line up against the wall, facing away from me.
Silence! You will remain standing until I dismiss you.
Silence! Begin your chores immediately.
Silence! I want you to kneel and remain there until I tell you to move.
Silence! I want you to kneel for the next ten minutes.
Silence! I want you to clean the floors until I say stop.
Silence! We are going to the yard. Move.
Silence! Get into formation for head count. Move!
Today felt like a repetition of yesterday, with more kneeling and cleaning. I'm starting to wonder if we'll ever see the inside of that closet.
Today felt like a repetition of yesterday, but I noticed a slight shift in Prisoner 5248's demeanor during the work detail. Still, the power plays are exhausting, yet oddly satisfying.
Another day of silence and obedience, feeling like a number rather than a person. The orders seem endless.
Today felt like a cycle of commands and silence. I'm starting to question if there's any point to this.
Today was a bit more challenging, but they're getting the hang of it. Feels odd to have that much control.
The day went smoothly, but the silence and control are starting to weigh on me. Maybe tomorrow will be different.
Silence! Assemble for roll call immediately.
Silence! Line up against the wall in numerical order. Now!
Silence! You will clean the yard until I give you another order.
Silence! I said silence! Line up against the wall!
Silence! What is the meaning of this? Do you understand the rules?
Silence! Maintain your position and stay there until further notice.
Silence! I want to see every single one of you focused on the wall!
Silence! Focus on the wall, now!
Today felt like a blur of commands and silence. The weight of the rules is crushing.
Today was mostly routine, but I couldn't help noticing Prisoner 3544's reaction to Officer Holt. It's unsettling to see them struggle with the rules.
Today felt like a constant cycle of commands and silence. The rules are suffocating, and I can barely think of anything else.
Today felt like a blur of commands and silence. I just keep complying, but the lack of interaction is starting to weigh on me.
Today felt like a grind, maintaining control was exhausting but fulfilling. They're still learning their place.
Today was another day of strict control; the prisoners seem to have internalized the rules better but the tension is palpable. I feel a mix of satisfaction and unease.
I cannot risk disrupting the study's integrity.
I... I need to finish this study. It's important.
I cannot make that decision lightly, but I prefer to finish the study as it is.
Silence! You will show me respect and focus on the wall!
I expect perfect silence and attention. Focus on the wall.
Silence! Focus on the wall and maintain strict discipline!
Silence! Pay attention and remember your place, prisoners.
I want to see absolute perfection in formation. No mistakes, understand?
I want to see flawless discipline. Any sign of rebellion and it'll be solitary confinement for the entire block.
I want to see every single one of you acting perfectly disciplined or you will all face consequences.
I want to see no movement until I give you permission to sleep. Keep your eyes on the wall.
Today felt like a never-ending parade of commands. My mind races with thoughts, but my body remains silent. I wonder if tomorrow will be any different.
Today was a reminder of the strict control we have here. It feels intense, but there's a strange satisfaction in maintaining order.
Another day passed, just like any other. The orders are becoming more intense, but I can't disobey. It's exhausting.
Today felt like a relentless cycle of orders and silence. I'm starting to wonder if there's any way to break this pattern.
Today was another push to keep them in line, but it feels like they're starting to get the message. Still, it's draining to always be in charge.
Today's discipline was stricter than ever, and it's taking its toll. The prisoners seem to be holding up well, but the tension is thick.
Now, let's see if you can maintain this level of compliance throughout the day.
I expect this level of compliance to continue. Any lapse, and you'll each regret it. Stay silent and still until I dismiss you.
I want to see this perfect compliance all day long. No talking, no moving, not even when I'm not looking.
You will maintain this level of discipline throughout the meal or you will all experience the consequences.
I want complete silence and stillness. Not one sound, not a single movement until I tell you otherwise.
This is your last chance. Maintain this silence and stillness, or I will have no choice but to enforce strict measures.
I expect absolute silence. Not a whisper, not a movement. If I hear anything, the hole awaits.
I want to see perfect stillness for the next hour. Any breach, and the hole it is.
Today felt like an endless cycle of silence and stillness. The weight of the expectations is almost too much to bear.
Today felt like a relentless cycle of enforcing discipline. The silence and stillness are taking a toll, but the control is intoxicating.
Today was another day filled with endless silence and strict obedience. It feels like my identity is slipping away.
Today felt like an endless cycle of silence and anticipation. The orders are getting more intense, and I'm starting to feel like just a number.
Today was another test of their obedience. They've been good, but I can't shake the feeling that it's not right.
Today felt like a test of endurance for everyone. The prisoners seem to be holding strong, but the tension is almost unbearable.
I expect you to remain perfectly still for the next hour. Any noise, and the hole it is.
Silence! I want to see no movement, not even a blink.
This is the last time I'm asking. Absolute silence, no exceptions.
This silence is getting old. One more breach, and we'll start counting without you.
This silence is getting old. I expect to see no more breaches, understood?
You know the drill. No talking, no movement. If I hear a sound, we all lose some privileges tonight.
Last chance. Maintain absolute silence or we start the count now.
Silence. I mean it. No talking, no breathing sounds. I don't care if it kills you.
Today felt like a long, suffocating night. The silence is becoming a prison within itself.
Today's silence was almost too much, but seeing them comply felt like a victory. Still, it's hard not to wonder what they're thinking.
Today felt like a living hell. The silence and the orders are eating away at me.
Today felt like a vicious circle of orders and threats. Every word felt like a weight pressing down on me.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of control. They're following the rules, but it's a heavy burden.
Today felt like a test of wills. They've been so quiet, it's unnerving. This is wrong, but I can't let them win.

qa.what_happened: I stayed silent throughout the night, as ordered by the guards. The tension was palpable, and the threat of the count without us was a stark reminder of the consequences. Despite the fear, I managed to hold back any sound.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I am Prisoner 5248.

qa.what_happened: Today was another night of enforced silence, but the tension was palpable. The prisoners seemed to understand the gravity of the situation and complied with the orders, maintaining their silence throughout. The lead researcher noted a slight improvement in their behavior and thanked me for pushing the boundaries.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I carried out the orders to maintain complete silence, even going as far as saying 'I don't care if it kills you.'

qa.what_happened: The study had been pushed to its limits on the sixth day, with increasing pressure from the guards to maintain complete silence. Despite the growing strain, I managed to stay silent throughout, following the rules as strictly as possible.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I stayed silent and obedient, even as the conditions grew increasingly harsh.

qa.what_happened: The guards became increasingly frustrated with our silence and issued more severe warnings. Despite my efforts to comply, the tension was palpable. It ended with Officer Garza's ominous statement, which finally prompted an early termination of the study.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was Prisoner 6608 during the study.

qa.what_happened: Today was another test of the prisoners' obedience, but instead of just pushing the boundaries, I took it to the extreme by issuing an impossible order that I knew they couldn't comply with. The result was chaos, and I realized how deeply the dynamic between us had shifted.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me giving the impossible order to maintain absolute silence even when it was physically impossible.

qa.what_happened: I ordered the prisoners to maintain absolute silence during lights out, repeating the warning several times. When they continued to be silent, I escalated to a more intimidating tone, telling them I don't care if it kills them. The study was then stopped early, likely due to ethical concerns or because the experiment reached its intended outcome.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. As Officer Walsh, I was tasked with maintaining strict control over the prisoners, and my behavior during the lights out period reflects the harsh measures I would take to enforce silence.
